source: Regulation (EU) 2017/745, Annex VIII (Classification Rules) and Article 2(65)/(66)/(68); see data/regulations/mdr_annex_classification_rules.txt and mdr_vigilance_articles.txt for full text

classification_overrides.reasoning: Rule 8: implantable devices are class IIb by default, but breast implants are explicitly listed as a class III exception.
Rule 8: surgical meshes are explicitly listed as a class III exception to the default class IIb for implantable devices.
Rule 8: total or partial joint replacements are class III, with the exception of ancillary components such as screws, wedges, plates and instruments.
Rule 8: spinal disc replacement implants and implantable devices in contact with the spinal column are class III, except ancillary components.
Rule 8: active implantable devices or their accessories are class III.
Rule 22: active therapeutic devices with an integrated diagnostic function that significantly determines patient management (e.g. closed-loop systems, AEDs) are class III.

classification_rules.criteria: All non-invasive devices, unless a more specific rule applies.
Non-invasive devices for channelling/storing blood, body liquids, cells or tissues for eventual infusion/administration. Blood bags are class IIb.

Non-invasive devices modifying biological/chemical composition of blood or body liquids for implantation/administration; filtration/centrifugation/gas-exchange only is class IIa; in-vitro contact with human embryos is class III.

Non-invasive devices contacting injured skin/mucous membrane: class I as mechanical barrier/compression/absorption; class IIb for secondary-intent chronic wound healing; class IIa for micro-environment management or other cases.
Invasive devices w.r.t. body orifices (non-surgical): class I transient, class IIa short-term, class IIb long-term (with oral/ear/nasal exceptions).
Surgically invasive, transient use: class IIa default; class I if reusable surgical instrument; class III if heart/CNS/central circulatory contact.
Surgically invasive, short-term use: class IIa default; class III for heart/CNS/circulatory contact; class IIb for ionising radiation, absorbable, or medicine administration.

Implantable / long-term surgically invasive: class IIb default; class III for heart/CNS/circulatory contact, breast implants, surgical meshes, joint replacements, spinal disc/spinal column implants, active implantables.
Active therapeutic devices administering/exchanging energy: class IIa default, class IIb if potentially hazardous energy exchange; class III if controlling active implantables.

Active diagnostic/monitoring devices: class IIa default; class IIb for vital-parameter monitoring where variation could cause immediate danger, or diagnosis in immediate-danger situations, or diagnostic/therapeutic radiology.

Diagnostic/therapeutic decision-support software: class IIa default; class IIb if decision error could cause serious deterioration/surgery; class III if decision error could cause death/irreversible deterioration.
Active devices administering/removing medicinal products, body liquids or substances: class IIa default, class IIb if potentially hazardous mode of administration.
All other active devices not covered by Rules 9-12.
Devices incorporating an ancillary medicinal substance.
Contraception / STD-prevention devices: class IIb default, class III if implantable or long-term invasive.
Contact lens disinfecting/cleaning/hydrating: class IIb; device sterilising/disinfecting solutions: class IIa (class IIb if end-point disinfection of invasive devices).
Devices recording diagnostic X-ray images.
Devices from non-viable human/animal tissues or cells, unless animal-derived and intact-skin-contact only.
Devices incorporating nanomaterial: class III high/medium internal exposure, IIb low, IIa negligible.
Inhaled medicinal product administration devices: class IIa default, class IIb if mode of action critical or life-threatening condition.
Substance-based devices absorbed by or dispersed in the body: class III if systemically absorbed, class IIa if skin/oral-pharynx local action, class IIb otherwise.
Active therapeutic devices with integrated diagnostic function significantly determining patient management (e.g. closed-loop systems, AEDs).

criteria.description: The incident directly or indirectly led, might have led, or might lead to the death of a patient, user or other person.

The incident directly or indirectly led, might have led, or might lead to the temporary or permanent serious deterioration of a patient's, user's, or other person's state of health, including hospitalization, prolonged hospitalization, permanent impairment, or need for medical/surgical intervention to prevent permanent damage.
The incident constitutes a serious public health threat: an event that could result in imminent risk of death, serious deterioration in health, or serious illness, requiring prompt remedial action.

non_serious_indicators: expected and documented side effect already quantified in technical documentation
near-miss with no patient contact or impact
device malfunction detected and resolved before use with no patient exposure

rules.description: Immediately, no later than 2 days after the manufacturer becomes aware of the threat.
Immediately after causal relationship is established or suspected, no later than 10 days after awareness.
Immediately after causal relationship is established or reasonably possible, no later than 15 days after awareness.
Periodic trend reporting per Article 88 for statistically significant increases in non-serious incident frequency/severity; observation period defined in the manufacturer's PMS plan.
